description:
## Overview

This PR adds the "Supported by Posit" badge to the waldo website.

## Background

We've recently started adding a "Supported by Posit" badge across all Posit package websites to create a more cohesive brand presence. The badge appears on the far right of the top navigation bar or at the bottom of the hamburger menu. It links to Posit’s main website. @hadley is involved with this initiative.

The following websites already have the "Supported by Posit" badge: [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org), [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/articles/intro.html), [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com), [Plotnine](https://plotnine.org), [Pointblank](https://posit-dev.github.io/pointblank/), [pointblank](https://rstudio.github.io/pointblank/), and [Quarto](https://quarto.org).

See https://posit-dev.github.io/supported-by-posit/ for more information.

## Changes

- Added a line to `_pkgdown.yml` to include the JavaScript file
- Standardized indentation in `_pkgdown.yml`

include is.nan()-comparison in num_equal() + test
description:
Accordingly to `?is.na`  comparing NA_real_ and NaN is not exactly straight forward. It is stated future CPU-architectures may confound NA_real_ and NaN. 

Accordingly to `?is.nan` `identical()` or equality should not be used to check for `NaN`

Proposed solution is to test if `is.nan(NA_real_) == is.nan(NaN)`
... and as long as this base function can tell the difference, so there is a difference.

Making waldo more strict, will likely require some R packages using testthat to update some tests.

My personal angle on this problem is I use testthat to verify my interface between Rust and R. I test if my mappings are isotone(reversible) in respect to `NaN` and `NA_real_`.

Fixes #150

title: Add compare options and allow them to be attached to objects.
description:
This is intended to fix #72, though there are some issues for discussion.

It adds options to `compare()` so it can ignore the order of names, ignore `NULL` elements in lists, or ignore specifically named components of lists.

The options can be attached as attributes to `x` or `y`, rather than being specified in the `compare(x, y)` call.

Some issues:

 - If the same option is specified in more than one place, what happens?  I chose to let one spec override earlier ones.  They are applied in the order:  defaults to `compare()`, options on `x`, options on `y`, user-specified arguments to `compare()`.  If `x` and `y` are lists, each component can change the options; the more specific one wins (just like CSS). You might want to change some of that. - 
- The `ignore_private = character()` option ignores components by name.  Because of the inheritance, this is kind of weird in nested structures:  maybe I'd just want to ignore `private` at one level but not others.  I can do this, but it's cumbersome.  Or maybe I'd like to specify a pattern for private components, instead of listing them all by name.

title: [FOR DISCUSSION] Diffobj 0.3.4 Compatibility
description:
This stems from https://github.com/brodieG/diffobj/issues/152.

Unfortunately the fix requires some changes shown here so that `waldo` behaves as intended.  I ended up changing the bailout algorithm to be more robust, and it does lead to a difference in one of the tests.  These tests are skipped on CRAN because they are `snapshot` tests[^1] so I don't think there is anything to do immediately unless folks start complaining about their `waldo` output changing.

With `max.diffs=1` we give the Myers algorithm one diff.  Under the new implementation it takes advantage of that to find one diff and a few matches, which makes the final diff different than an element by element one.  To get the element by element one we really need to set `max.diffs=0`.  Presumably you tried that previously but it didn't work because 0 was an undocumented alias for -1 (a mistake, really).

Diffobj 0.3.4 ([release candidate][2]) now really treats `max.diffs=0` as "immediately fall back to naive algorithm".

I'm going to hold off on CRAN submission for now in case you have any feedback on this.

[^1]: I took me a while to figure out what was going on with the skipped tests as searching for "skip" and "cran" and such lead to nothing.  Probably annoying to do but might be worth having a "skipped snapshot" or such reporting category to make this more obvious.
[2]: https://github.com/brodieG/diffobj/releases/tag/rc-0.3.4-v1

title: Use identical() for fast path
description:
Fixes #86

This radically improves performance (I suspect generally making it generally faster than `all.equal()` in the no difference case), particularly for the motivating example, which previously took 2s on my machine:

``` r
library(sf)
#> Linking to GEOS 3.8.1, GDAL 3.1.4, PROJ 6.3.1

sf_points <- do.call(st_sfc, lapply(1:1000, function(x) st_point(runif(2))))
sf_points_copy <- st_as_sfc(st_as_binary(sf_points))

bench::mark(
  waldo::compare(sf_points_copy, sf_points),
  all.equal(sf_points_copy, sf_points),
  identical(sf_points_copy, sf_points),
  check = FALSE
)
#> Warning: Some expressions had a GC in every iteration; so filtering is disabled.
#> # A tibble: 3 x 6
#>   expression                                     min  median `itr/sec` mem_alloc
#>   <bch:expr>                                <bch:tm> <bch:t>     <dbl> <bch:byt>
#> 1 waldo::compare(sf_points_copy, sf_points)   85.6µs  93.6µs    9315.      503KB
#> 2 all.equal(sf_points_copy, sf_points)        92.1ms  99.4ms      10.1     219KB
#> 3 identical(sf_points_copy, sf_points)        53.4µs  55.7µs   16751.         0B
#> # … with 1 more variable: gc/sec <dbl>
```

<sup>Created on 2021-07-11 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.0)</sup>

However, I need to think if there are edge cases (apart from `Encoding()`) where `identical()` returns `TRUE` and there are actually important differences.

Call `encodeString()` after computing the diff
description:
Closes #66 

I am fairly certain this placement is correct.

It seems that `encodeString()` is purely related to the formatting done in `format_diff_matrix()`, and is not related to computing the diff itself. Following that logic, it makes sense to only call `encodeString()` after the diff itself has been computed on the original strings. This fixes #66, since now the original strings aren't modified in any way (beyond the expected call to `enc2utf8()` in `ses()`).

I originally tried to move the `enc2utf8()` from `ses()` up into `diff_element()` before the call to `encodeString()`, but that would incorrectly print the formatted diffs in UTF-8, rather than in their original encoding. ~Since there was no test for this, I added one.~ (Update: Removed the test, see below)

I have confirmed that this fixes the vctrs build when using `rhub::local_check_linux(image = "rhub/debian-clang-devel")`
